result.summary: Disconnects only the misbehaving peer rather than all connections sharing an IP address when a peer is discouraged. In `PeerManagerImpl::MaybeDiscourageAndDisconnect`, it sets `fDisconnect = true` on the specific `CNode` instead of invoking `DisconnectNode` on an IP subnet, and removes the now-unused `disconnect_private_broadcast` parameter from `CConnman::DisconnectNode`.
result.problem: When a peer misbehaves and triggers discouragement, `MaybeDiscourageAndDisconnect` disconnects all inbound connections sharing the peer's IP address. For clearnet-over-Tor inbound connections, multiple peers share a Tor exit node's IP address, allowing an attacker to disconnect all honest inbound peers from the same exit node by sending an invalid message.
evidence: PR description: "If an attacker connects to the node through the same exit node and sends an invalid message, they can cause every inbound peer sharing the exit node's IP to get disconnected. Fix this by only disconnecting the misbehaving CNode rather than every CNode sharing the IP."
result.changed_since_previous: The diff also removes the unused disconnect_private_broadcast parameter from CConnman::DisconnectNode(const CSubNet&).
result.card: Prevents Bitcoin Core from disconnecting all peers sharing an IP address when a single misbehaving peer triggers discouragement. Currently, MaybeDiscourageAndDisconnect disconnects by IP subnet, allowing an attacker sharing a Tor exit node IP to intentionally drop all honest inbound connections using the same exit node. The change marks only the misbehaving connection for disconnection while still registering the IP address with the discouragement filter.

risk.why: A flaw in peer disconnect logic could cause misbehaving peers to remain connected or alter expected disconnection behaviour across network types.
